findings.title: ImageMagick downsize reads and writes the same path
findings.body: OptimizedImage.downsize is called with tempfile.path as both the source and the destination. convert_with shells out to ImageMagick `convert` (and ImageOptim) with those paths. ImageMagick truncates the output file before it finishes reading the input, so using one path for both commonly yields an empty or corrupt file. The upload then proceeds with that damaged tempfile, so large-image downsizing fails or stores a broken image instead of a reduced original.

findings.title: Second downsize definition overwrites the width/height API
findings.body: Ruby does not overload methods. The new downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts) at this line replaces the downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts) defined just above, so that width/height implementation is dead. Existing callers that pass numeric max width and height now treat the width as a geometry string and the height integer as opts. optimize then evaluates opts[:allow_animation] and raises NoMethodError, so thumbnail downsizing that still uses the old signature breaks.

findings.title: Upload size cap hardcoded to 10MB for every type
findings.body: validateUploadedFile used to enforce Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so images and attachments had separate admin-configured limits. It now always uses 10 * 1024. Attachments ignore max_attachment_size_kb (users can submit files the server should reject, or are blocked below a higher attachment limit). Images are also capped at 10MB even when max_image_size_kb is larger, so previously allowed uploads are rejected. displayErrorForUpload's 413 branch (line 246) has the same hardcode and will report 10MB even when the real limit is different.

findings.title: Downsize result is ignored and may never meet the size limit
findings.body: The loop calls OptimizedImage.downsize but discards its false return value, and -resize 80% changes pixel dimensions rather than targeting a byte size. If convert fails, the file is unchanged or corrupt and the loop still retries the same path. If it succeeds, five 80% passes (about 33% of each side) often leave a JPEG/PNG larger than SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb. The code then always calls Upload.create_for on whatever is left, so an upload that the client just allowed can still be over the configured limit or be a failed conversion, with no error from this step.

findings.title: Animated GIF downsize is passed a percentage geometry
findings.body: When SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails is on and the file is a GIF, downsize uses gifsicle --resize-fit with the geometry "80%". gifsicle's --resize-fit expects pixel dimensions such as WIDTHxHEIGHT, not an ImageMagick percentage. Those attempts fail (convert_with returns false), the bytes are not reduced, and animated uploads that are over max_image_size_kb are never actually downsized.
